chosenArchitecture: Monolithic Electron desktop app (Candidate A), hardened. One Electron main process (TypeScript) owns everything: the SQLite registry (better-sqlite3, WAL), the node-pty children, the xterm.js renderers, the transcript-tail watchers (chokidar), the sessions-cache scanner, the fusion state engine, and a unix-domain-socket hook endpoint. React 19 + Zustand renderer. Launched at login via macOS SMAppService LoginItem (the APP itself, not a separate daemon). The two changes that close Candidate A's stated adoption gap WITHOUT adding a daemon: (1) the installed hook shim (ccc-emit.sh) POSTs to the socket with a ~200ms budget and SPOOLS the event to ~/.claude/ccc/events/<sid>.ndjson on any failure, draining on next app start — so a closed app loses no working-edges and never errors a Claude turn; (2) adoption is a cold filesystem reconstruction (ps + sessions/<pid>.json + transcript-tail) run at launch and re-run on a periodic rescan while open, which needs no live listener because transcripts and the pid-cache exist on disk independent of any process. Stack: Electron 42.x + TypeScript; React 19 + Zustand; @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 + @xterm/addon-webgl + @xterm/addon-fit + @xterm/addon-serialize; node-pty 1.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.x in the main process (both rebuilt via @electron/rebuild); chokidar v4; @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 for the per-session Channels server.
justification: The decision hinges on whether the ADOPTION requirement truly needs an always-on daemon. It does not, and this is the load-bearing analysis. Adopted sessions (the ~19 already live) never had our hooks installed — hooks bind at session start (verified in the state-engine doc), so no SessionStart or working-edge hook ever fires into ANY listener for them, daemon or not. Their entire live-status story is the transcript-tail watcher + the sessions/<pid>.json cache + a ps liveness guard — all of which read FILES THAT EXIST ON DISK INDEPENDENT OF ANY RUNNING PROCESS. A launch-time cold scan reconstructs their full state; a periodic rescan while the app is open catches sessions a user starts in iTerm meanwhile. An always-on daemon would add live monitoring only for sessions the TOOL launched — but the app owns those PTYs, so they die the moment the window closes (F2: no live process survives app-close/reboot on any substrate). There is therefore nothing live for a daemon to monitor while the app is closed; the daemon's supposed benefit evaporates against the actual facts. Candidate A's own two cons are both neutralized cheaply: (a) the 'hooks POST to a dead socket errors every Claude turn' footgun is eliminated by the disk-spool fail-open shim the state-engine design already specifies (200ms budget, exit 0 fast, spool-and-drain) — this is required regardless of daemon; (b) the 'no tracking while closed' con only matters for tool-launched sessions whose processes are dead anyway, and for adopted sessions the cold rescan covers it. Against the six requirements: 1 CONTAINMENT and 4 NAVIGATION are renderer concerns identical on any process model. 2 STATUS SPACE and 3 HIERARCHY are satisfied by the in-process fusion engine + SQLite registry (the two docs I read are written against exactly an Electron main process — they are internally consistent with A, not with a Rust/Tauri backend). 5 RESUME is registry-driven relaunch of claude --resume + serialize snapshot, identical on every candidate (no substrate survives reboot). 6 CROSS-SESSION SEND uses per-session Channels servers spawned by the app for tool-launched sessions and send-keys for adopted — the app owning the PTYs is what makes send-keys reachable at all, which a headless daemon complicates. Against buildability-with-Claude (the stated priority): A is the densest-training-data path — Electron + TS + xterm.js + node-pty is the VS Code/Hyper stack — with ONE process, ONE language, NO IPC wire protocol, NO launchd plist, NO SMAppService daemon-approval flow, NO second DB writer. Electron over Tauri because both on-disk designs assume node-pty and the watchers run in-process JS; Tauri would rewrite PTY handling in Rust (portable-pty over the v2 Channel API) and split the state engine across a JS/Rust boundary — novel surface a Claude-maintained codebase should avoid, for a memory saving that is not the stated priority. The WebGL/xterm contract (pin 6.0.0, WebGL-only since canvas was removed, ~16-context visible-only render) is identical on both, so Tauri buys nothing on the terminal side. Net: A meets all six requirements, fully satisfies adoption once hardened with spool+rescan, and is the most reliable thing Claude can author and maintain.
rejectedAndWhy: Candidate B (Electron UI over a separate long-lived launchd daemon) — REJECTED. Its one real advantage over hardened-A is capturing SessionStart hooks and working-edges for tool-launched sessions while the UI is closed. But those sessions' PTYs are owned by the process tree and die on app-close/reboot (F2), so there is no live session to monitor while closed; and for the ~19 ADOPTED sessions the daemon gains literally nothing because no hooks fire for them regardless (hooks bind at session start, pre-install) — their status comes from on-disk transcripts a cold scan reads anyway. So the daemon's cost (a second OS process, a JSON-RPC/WebSocket wire contract between UI and daemon, PTY-byte streaming over that socket, daemon supervision/restart, a launchd LaunchAgent or SMAppService approval that macOS 13+ surfaces to the user as a Login Item with a TCC prompt, and a two-writer SQLite story) buys a benefit that the disk-spool shim + launch/periodic rescan already deliver in A. It also raises buildability risk sharply: it is the design with the most moving parts for Claude to author and keep coherent, and the PTY-ownership question ('daemon owns PTYs and streams bytes to the UI xterm') is the single most complex and least-trodden piece in any candidate. Reconsider ONLY if a future requirement demands headless monitoring of sessions with NO UI ever open (e.g. server-side status for a team) — not the case here (single-user macOS desktop). Candidate C (fork cmux native-Swift/libghostty GPL, or opcode/Claudia Tauri/Rust AGPL) — REJECTED on buildability and license. A Swift/libghostty base abandons the entire node-pty/xterm/chokidar/better-sqlite3 toolchain all four design docs are written against, forcing a rewrite of the state engine, registry, and Channels integration in a stack with far thinner Claude training data; GPL/AGPL also encumbers a personal tool the user may not want copyleft-bound. The forks' head start is in terminal-hosting, which xterm.js 6.0 + WebGL already solves for A per F4.
pinnedLibraries: electron 42.x (current stable line, e.g. 42.5.2; the 'Electron 3x' in the candidate text was loose — real stable is 42.x)
@xterm/xterm >= 6.0.0 (pin 6.0.0 exactly — DEC private mode 2026 synchronized output; canvas renderer removed in 6.0 so WebGL is the only accelerated renderer)
node-pty 1.1.0 (in Electron main process; no prebuilt for newest Electron — rebuild required)
better-sqlite3 12.x (12.11.1 current; WAL mode; native, shares the rebuild step)
chokidar 4.x (v4 bundles fsevents and drops the glob dep; v5 is ESM-only/Node-20+ and fights Electron CJS main)
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 (per-session Channels server; MCP v2 SDK stable lands 2026-07-28 — plan a migration point, do not target v2 pre-release now)
@electron/rebuild (build-time; rebuild node-pty + better-sqlite3 + fsevents on every Electron/Node ABI bump)

topRisks.risk: Channels research-preview + open bug #71792 (dev-flag channel notifications silently dropped) may make the primary INJECT path non-functional on current builds; also requires claude.ai login, no API-key auth.
topRisks.mitigation: Prove it in Spike 0 before building on it; keep send-keys inject-then-verify as the always-present fallback via the registry sendCapability field; version-gate per cc_version; ship v1 on send-keys if the bug blocks it and flip to Channels at GA.

topRisks.risk: node-pty + better-sqlite3 are native modules with no prebuilt for Electron 42.x; every ABI bump breaks launch until rebuilt.
topRisks.mitigation: Pin Electron/Node exactly; @electron/rebuild as postinstall + CI gate rebuilding node-pty, better-sqlite3, fsevents together; startup ABI self-check with a clear remediation message.

topRisks.risk: Transcript JSONL and sessions/<pid>.json are internal/undocumented and version-spread (2.1.162–2.1.201); a format drift can silently break waiting/idle detection, on which the whole status board depends.
topRisks.mitigation: Versioned defensive parser (try/catch per line, backward-scan to last real record, skip isSidechain), mtime-only fallback so the board degrades not goes dark, per-node cc_version gating, and the STUCK watchdog as a format-independent backstop.

topRisks.risk: WebGL ~16-context cap with canvas removed in xterm 6.0 means WebGL-or-nothing; ~19 sessions will exhaust contexts if all rendered.
topRisks.mitigation: VS Code visible-only model from day one (is_open flag, buffered/detached backgrounded PTYs, serialize-snapshot for non-live nodes, hard cap on simultaneous live terminals); test at 19+ nodes.

topRisks.risk: send-keys is brittle (bracketed-paste, multiline, vim NORMAL, Esc-Esc corruption, version-dependent CR) and often unreachable for truly external adopted sessions, so some cross-sends are unsupported until relaunch.
topRisks.mitigation: Inject-then-VERIFY every send by reading the pane back; classify sendCapability (channel|pty-sendkeys|external-degraded) and surface external-degraded plainly with one-click restart-under-management; never silently no-op.

topRisks.risk: Installing hooks by editing shared ~/.claude/settings.json can clobber existing global hooks (dirty-tree-guard, usage-governor), statusline, and mcpServers already load-bearing on this machine.
topRisks.mitigation: Additive-merge installer: append matcher-groups (never rewrite), identify our groups by the ccc-emit.sh substring so re-install replaces only ours, backup before first write, tmp+fsync+atomic-rename; prefer session/project-scope registration over global edits where possible.

riskiestFirstBuildOrder: SPIKE 0 — Terminal-host + Channels proof (prove the two biggest unknowns before any app scaffolding). In a throwaible Electron main process: pin @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 + WebGL + FitAddon, spawn a real `claude` via node-pty 1.1.0 with TERM=xterm-256color, and confirm the Claude Code TUI renders cleanly — spinner, alt-screen, no scroll/garble — through a resize that recomputes cols/rows and calls pty.resize() (SIGWINCH). In the SAME spike, spawn one claude with our @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 channel server + --dangerously-load-development-channels and prove an inbound notification actually lands in-session and cc_ack round-trips (directly tests bug #71792). Also rebuild node-pty via @electron/rebuild against Electron 42.x here. If any of these three fail, the whole architecture assumption is wrong — find out on day one, not week six.

SPIKE 1 — State-engine truth on live data. Build the transcript-tail watcher (chokidar v4, backward-scan to last real record, skip isSidechain, mtime staleness) + the unix-socket hook endpoint + disk-spool shim, and run it against the ~19 REAL live sessions on this machine. Prove coarse WORKING/WAITING/IDLE/STUCK is correct for both a tool-launched session (hooks fire) and an adopted session (transcript-only). This validates that adoption works WITHOUT a daemon — the core bet of the chosen architecture.

2 — Registry foundation: better-sqlite3 schema (session/edge/category/handoff_note/scrollback_snapshot/status_event), node-id vs claude_session_id split, migrations, single-writer rule. Everything else persists through this.

3 — Adoption pipeline: ps + sessions/<pid>.json reconciliation with the lstart PID-reuse guard and the args-regex claude matcher, transcript self-identification, degraded-mode nodes in a holding zone. This makes the ~19 appear — highest user-visible value and it exercises the no-daemon adoption path end to end.

4 — Resume-on-restart: scrollback capture (addon-serialize, 1000-line cap, idle-debounce + on-quit), reconcile-then-relaunch (attach if pid still alive after mere app-restart, else claude --resume), deleted-transcript recovery. Proves requirement 5 and the spool-drain path.

5 — Managed-launch path shared by spawn/resume/adopt-restart: wires the additive settings.json hook merge (backup + atomic rename + ccc-emit.sh idempotency tag) and the per-session Channels server + token-gated unix socket.
6 — Cross-send: tiered send() dispatch on sendCapability (Channels primary, send-keys inject-then-VERIFY fallback), then COPY/SHARE/BROADCAST.

7 — UI polish: React/Zustand shell — beacon bar (global cross-category board), category rail, indented tree with typed-edge rendering and blocked-parent banner, keyboard-first navigation, then drag-to-reparent and the WebGL visible-only render budget.

8 — Precision add-ons (M2): split WAITING_PERMISSION out of WAITING via Notification:permission_prompt fast edges + on-demand PTY-scrape tie-breaker; out-of-tool ppid-chain parent inference as confirm-only suggestions.
